title: bug: JetBrains Accounts launch still resolves bare powershell or WSL node at the project cwd
description: Residual explicitly excluded from task-b071e3bf: TerminalAgentLauncher.buildAccountsCommand uses powerShellLine's bare powershell default on Windows and literal `node ` under WSL, even for protected projects. A project powershell.bat in a Command Prompt terminal, or project node on an in-project PATH entry, can run before the selected Accounts CLI. Pin and validate trusted interpreters without changing legacy lines; account for WSL node having no fixed system path.
definitionOfDone: Protected Accounts launch never resolves its interpreter through project cwd or unsafe PATH; refusal launches nothing.
Legacy Accounts lines remain byte-identical and tests cover native Windows and WSL refusal/selection.

implementationPlan.description:
The protected WSL route, in moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/TerminalAgentLauncher.kt, with the Edit tool. Builders stay pure: no I/O.

1. Next to buildAccountsCommand (:549), declare the program on ONE line: `internal const val PROTECTED_WSL_NODE_PROGRAM = "..."`.
- Use a normal Kotlin string whose line ends with its closing quote. Escape each `"` as `\"` and each `$` as `\$`. Step 4's probe extracts it with sed, so keep this exact form.
- The value, byte for byte (523 characters):
`f() { echo "[ERROR] MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND: node was not found on an absolute PATH entry outside the project; refusing to start." >&2; exit 1; }; p=$(cd -- "$1" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || f; shift; k=; IFS=: read -r -a e <<< "$PATH"; for d in "${e[@]}"; do case $d in /*) ;; *) continue ;; esac; r=$(cd -- "$d" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || continue; u=$r; while :; do [ "$u" -ef "$p" ] && continue 2; [ "$u" = / ] && break; u=${u%/*}; u=${u:-/}; done; k=${k:+$k:}$r; done; [ -n "$k" ] || f; PATH=$k; exec node "$@"`
- Put a short comment above it:
  - builtins only;
  - the same rule as protected_trusted_dir in scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-call.sh (task-0b2ea570): keep absolute PATH entries whose real path is neither the project nor under it, as real paths, in order, walking ancestors with `-ef` so a link cannot hide the project;
  - keeping nothing refuses, because an empty PATH makes bash search the cwd, which is the project;
  - then it execs node, so WSL's node, which has no fixed system path, is found only outside the project.

2. Add `private fun protectedAccountsRefusal(reason: String): Nothing`. It throws IllegalArgumentException("Protected execution profile: $reason. Moe runs account commands only with an interpreter outside the project, so nothing was started.").

3. Add `private fun protectedWslAccountsCommand(cli: AccountCli, registryFile: String, args: List<String>, basePath: String): String`.
- Refuse unless basePath starts with a drive letter, a colon, and a slash or backslash (Regex `^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]`). The reason is "the project $basePath has no /mnt path in WSL, so WSL's node cannot be checked against it". UNC, rooted, drive-relative, POSIX and empty basePaths all refuse here.
- project = toWslPath(basePath). Pass every typed word (project, toWslPath(cli.script), toWslPath(registryFile) and each arg) through requireSafeArg("accounts command word", ...).
- The word is protectedInterpreter(ScriptKind.BASH, wslAgents = true, basePath, windows = true), which is Ready("/bin/bash"); on Refused, refuse with its reason. The WSL_BASH shell exists only on a Windows host, so windows = true is literally true, and the A5 pin stays host-independent.
- Return `shQuote(word) + " -c " + shQuote(PROTECTED_WSL_NODE_PROGRAM) + " moe-accounts " + shQuote(project) + " " + (listOf(toWslPath(cli.script), "--accounts-file", toWslPath(registryFile)) + args).joinToString(" ") { shQuote(it) }`.
- cli.node is not typed on this route. As today, WSL's own node runs the CLI, so claude signs in where WSL agents run it.

Error handling:
- A refusal or a control character throws IllegalArgumentException before any line exists.
- Inside WSL, a missing node outside the project prints `[ERROR] MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND ...` and exits 1 before any node runs. The IDE cannot see WSL's PATH, so that refusal happens in the opened tab.
implementationPlan.note: Added PROTECTED_WSL_NODE_PROGRAM (one line, sed-extracted bytes equal the plan's 523-char value), protectedAccountsRefusal, protectedWslAccountsCommand (drive-qualified basePath regex, requireSafeArg on every typed word, word from protectedInterpreter(BASH, wslAgents=true, windows=true)). The step-4 WSL probe already passes against the source: 'WSL probe: outside node selected; 3 refusals ran no node'.

implementationPlan.description:
Native routes and the dispatch, in moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/TerminalAgentLauncher.kt, with the Edit tool.

1. protectedInterpreter (:130) gets a last parameter `subject: String = "the agent wrapper's interpreter"`. Its two path messages become "$subject $candidate is not an absolute regular file outside the project" and "$subject ${file.path} holds a character a terminal cannot take unquoted". The default keeps b071e3bf's text, so P1-P3 stay green unchanged.

2. buildAccountsCommand (:549) gets `interpreter: String? = null`. Only the POWERSHELL arm uses it: `powerShellLine(<the unchanged "& " + psQuoted words>, interpreter ?: "powershell")`. The WSL_BASH and BASH arms are unchanged. Legacy callers pass nothing, so their bytes are identical. Mention the parameter in the KDoc.

3. Add `internal fun accountsCommandFor(profile: RuntimeProfile, cli: AccountCli, registryFile: String, args: List<String>, shell: AccountsShell, basePath: String, systemRoot: String? = System.getenv("SystemRoot")): String`.
- LEGACY: `return buildAccountsCommand(cli, registryFile, args, shell)`, and nothing else.
- PROTECTED node check, used by BASH and POWERSHELL: RuntimeSelectionPolicy.installedExecutable(cli.node, basePath). Accepted gives selection.file.path, the real path. Rejected gives protectedAccountsRefusal("the Accounts command's node ${cli.node} is not an absolute regular file outside the project"). Never pass on installedExecutable's own node-labelled text.
- BASH (native POSIX): `buildAccountsCommand(cli.copy(node = <real node>), registryFile, args, shell)`. The first typed word is that absolute real path, so no PATH or cwd lookup happens.
- POWERSHELL (native Windows):
  - word = protectedInterpreter(ScriptKind.POWERSHELL, wslAgents = false, basePath, systemRoot = systemRoot, subject = "the Accounts command's PowerShell"); Refused gives protectedAccountsRefusal(reason);
  - then the node check;
  - return `buildAccountsCommand(cli.copy(node = <real node>), registryFile, args, shell, interpreter = word)`. It types the forward-slash System32 powershell.exe that QA verified for b071e3bf in cmd, PowerShell 5.1 and Git Bash.
- WSL_BASH: protectedWslAccountsCommand(cli, registryFile, args, basePath), from step 2.

4. accountsCommandLine (:563): `val basePath = project.basePath ?: ""`, then `accountsCommandFor(RuntimeSelectionPolicy.profile(basePath), cli, registryFile, args, accountsShellFor(SystemInfo.isWindows, isWslAgentsEnabled(project)), basePath)`.
- profile("") is LEGACY, so a project with no path keeps today's line.
- profile() is the reader that seat launches use, so the downgrade pin and prompt apply the same way.

5. runAccountsCommand (:572): keep `val line = accountsCommandLine(...)` as its first statement, before resolveTerminalManager.
- Extend its KDoc: it also throws IllegalArgumentException, before any tab opens, when the protected profile has no trusted interpreter.
- AccountsPanel.runCli (AccountsPanel.kt:310-328) already turns that into one error dialog, and it types and copies nothing. Do not edit AccountsPanel.kt.
- Its no-terminal copy fallback calls accountsCommandLine again, so it can only copy a protected line.

Error handling: installedExecutable and protectedInterpreter never throw. Every refusal is the single IllegalArgumentException from protectedAccountsRefusal, and it is raised before any terminal manager, widget or clipboard is touched.

AccountsPanel.kt untouched. Tests run in step 4's gate.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Under the protected profile, the JetBrains Accounts tab never starts the accounts CLI through an interpreter found by the project cwd or an unsafe PATH entry. Native Windows types <SystemRoot>/System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell.exe in forward-slash form, and its decoded script runs the real path of the daemon's node, validated as an absolute regular file outside the project. Native POSIX types that validated real node path as the first word. WSL agent mode types /bin/bash -c with a builtins-only program. The program keeps only absolute PATH entries whose real path is outside the project, refuses with MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND when none is kept or the project does not resolve, and then execs node. An IDE-side refusal throws IllegalArgumentException before any terminal or clipboard is touched, so AccountsPanel shows one error dialog and types and copies nothing. Under LEGACY every Accounts line is byte-identical.
acceptanceCriteria: A1: accountsCommandFor(LEGACY, ...) equals buildAccountsCommand(...) for every AccountsShell, and every existing legacy Accounts pin in TerminalAgentLauncherTest and AccountPresentationTest passes unchanged.

A2 and A3 (Windows): the protected PowerShell line starts with the forward-slash fixture powershell.exe, and its decoded script equals the legacy script with the validated node. An unset, blank, in-project, untypable or missing SystemRoot refuses, naming SystemRoot or the path and the Accounts subject, and so does an in-project node.
A4: on the BASH route an outside node gives the legacy-shaped line with its real path, and a relative, bare, in-project, missing or directory node refuses, naming it.

A5 and A6: the protected WSL line is exactly '/bin/bash' -c '<PROTECTED_WSL_NODE_PROGRAM>' moe-accounts '<project /mnt path>' plus the quoted /mnt script, flag, registry and args. The program has no single quote, backslash, '!', C0 or DEL. A UNC, POSIX, drive-relative or empty basePath refuses, and a control character keeps the existing message.

A7 (POSIX, CI) and step 4's WSL probe (local): the program selects the outside node over '.', empty, relative, in-project and symlinked in-project entries, passes arguments intact, and refuses with exit 1 and no node run when only unsafe entries remain, when a relative entry would point outside, or when the project is missing.
The new rows fail on today's bytes (RED recorded), and mutants k1, k2 and the program's empty-keep guard are killed.
invariants: Under PROTECTED no Accounts line starts with a bare powershell or node, and none of its interpreters is looked up through the project cwd or an empty, '.', relative or in-project PATH entry.
A refusal throws before resolveTerminalManager, createTerminalWidget or the clipboard, because runAccountsCommand computes the line first.
Builders stay pure string functions. On the IDE side only installedExecutable and protectedInterpreter touch the file system.
PROTECTED_WSL_NODE_PROGRAM runs bash builtins only before exec node, and stays one Kotlin line whose value is free of single quotes, backslashes and '!'.
compatibility: LEGACY Accounts lines are byte-identical: accountsCommandFor's LEGACY branch returns buildAccountsCommand unchanged, and buildAccountsCommand's new interpreter parameter defaults to the bare powershell word.
protectedInterpreter's default subject keeps b071e3bf's messages, and P1-P3, PINNED_LEGACY, RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest and VerifiedLocalLaunchTest pass unchanged.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
WSL node has no fixed system path (apt, NodeSource, nvm, volta, brew), so no IDE-side pin exists. Rejected:
(1) Refuse every protected WSL Accounts launch. Protected WSL seats are supported (b071e3bf pins /bin/bash for them), so this would strand their sign-in.
(2) A fixed PATH of /usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin. It breaks nvm and volta node, and claude in ~/.local/bin.
(3) Ask wsl.exe for node's path at click time. It is slow, and the answer can change before the line runs.
(4) Ship a new installed helper script. That means bundling plus ps1/sh parity for one line of logic.
Chosen: an inline, builtins-only bash program typed after the absolute /bin/bash. It applies the wrappers' protected_trusted_dir rule (task-0b2ea570) and then runs exec node. Its scrubbed PATH is also what the CLI's claude inherits.
Native Windows reuses b071e3bf's protectedInterpreter for the PowerShell word. The node is checked with installedExecutable, which costs nothing.
Refusal channel: an IllegalArgumentException, which AccountsPanel already turns into one dialog with nothing typed or copied. That keeps AccountsPanel.kt unchanged and the plan at 2 files.
I filed two residual rows instead of widening this one: task-55710898 (the accounts CLI's own claude lookup) and task-a6227f4e (the VS Code twin).

planningNotes.risks:
- Kotlin string templates: every $ in the program must be escaped as \$, and the declaration must stay on one line, or step 4's sed extraction fails (it fails loudly).
- The typed program must stay free of ', backslash and !, because fish treats backslashes inside single quotes as escapes.
- The WSL refusal runs inside the opened tab: the IDE cannot read WSL's PATH. It prints MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND and exits 1 before any node runs.
- A7 skips on the Windows gate by design, so the WSL probe in step 4 is the local behavioural evidence. CI's ubuntu job runs A7.
- profile() may show the downgrade prompt from the Accounts tab, as seat launches already do.
- A project opened through a subst or alias drive passes its alias /mnt path. That is the same exposure as the WSL seat's --project, so it is not widened here.
